newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot residual prices unchanged in thin talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot residual prices unchanged in thin talk.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices ended Wednesday unchanged against Tuesday's levels in thin talk amid lackluster end-user demand and steady bunker fuel activity, market sources said.

"There's not a lot of demand," said a East Coast utility buyer, referring to its scant need for 0.3 percent sulphur resid, which was about one dollar per million British thermal units more expensive to natural gas.
However, a upstate New York utility was heard seeking 100,000 barrels of 0.7 and 100,000 barrels of 1.5 percent sulphur materials for delivery in October.
NYH physical one percent were again near $19.00 a barrel, with early October paper quote at $19.55-$19.80 on strength in crude oil futures, up from from Monday's $19.20-$19.50.
NYMEX November crude futures settled down nine cents at $24.05 and November Henry Hub natgas futures ended down 0.5 cents at $2.180/mmBtu.
At the Gulf, one percent sulphur grade was unchanged at $17.50 and three percent was valued flat at $17.25.
October New York City Gate gas was assessed little changed Tuesday at near the $2.22-$2.26/mmBtu, compared with NYH one percent resid at $3.02/mmBtu equivalent.
